title: Unbounded derived sections agree with localized-site derived sections
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in a common universe containing its objects, arrows, covering families and coefficient values [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Write $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ for its category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $W$ be an object of $\mathcal C$. Give $\mathcal C/W$ the localized topology, put $\mathcal O_W=\mathcal O|_W$, and let $j_W^*$ denote sectionwise restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Use unbounded cochain derived categories and total right derived functors computed by K-injective resolutions [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O))$, let $R\Gamma(W,K)$ be derived evaluation at $W$, followed by forgetting scalars, and let $R\Gamma(\mathcal C/W,j_W^*K)$ be derived evaluation at the final object $\mathrm{id}_W$ of the slice, also followed by forgetting scalars. There is a canonical isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$, natural in $K$, $$R\Gamma(W,K)\cong R\Gamma(\mathcal C/W,j_W^*K).$$ For any K-injective representative $I$ of $K$, this isomorphism is represented by the degreewise identity $I(W)=(I|_W)(\mathrm{id}_W)$. In particular, for every integer $q$, $$H^qR\Gamma(W,K)\cong H^qR\Gamma(\mathcal C/W,j_W^*K).$$ No boundedness of $K$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0D6F, lemma-unbounded-cohomology-of-open, statement and K-injective proof; canonical complex identification in that proof

proof.text: The underlying categories of $\mathcal C$ and of $\mathcal C/W$ are small (an object of $\mathcal C/W$ is an arrow $V\to W$ of $\mathcal C$), and $\mathcal O$, $\mathcal O_W$ are sheaves of commutative rings, so [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] applies on both sites: $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ and $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_W)$ have K-injective resolutions. Hence the right-derived-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] applies to the additive functors of evaluation at $W$ and at $\operatorname{id}_W$ (followed by forgetting scalars): their total right derived functors on the unbounded derived categories are computed by applying the functor termwise to a K-injective resolution. Choose a K-injective cochain complex $I$ representing $K$. Apply [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized] with the ring sheaf $\mathcal O$ and object $W$: the termwise restriction $I|_W$, which represents $j_W^*K$, is K-injective on the localized ringed site. Hence $R\Gamma(W,K)$ is represented by the complex $I(W)$, while $R\Gamma(\mathcal C/W,j_W^*K)$ is represented by $(I|_W)(\operatorname{id}_W)$.

source.place: Tags 08FI and 0D6F; choose a K-injective representative and restrict it

proof.text: By the sectionwise definition of localized restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], for every degree $n$ one has $I^n(W)=((I|_W)^n)(\operatorname{id}_W)$, and the restriction of the differential $d_I^n$ at $\operatorname{id}_W$ is exactly $d_I^n(W)$. Thus the two displayed representatives are the same cochain complex after forgetting scalars, and the comparison is the degreewise identity.

The identity in the preceding step commutes with every chain map. A morphism $K\to K'$ of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O))$ between objects represented by K-injective complexes $I,I'$ is the class of a chain map $f:I\to I'$, unique up to homotopy, by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; its restriction $f|_W$ represents $j_W^*$ of that morphism, and $(f|_W)(\operatorname{id}_W)=f(W)$ as maps of complexes. Taking $f$ a quasi-isomorphism between two K-injective representatives of $K$ shows that the identification does not depend on the representative. Since both sides are the total right derived functors computed on K-injectives by [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], this strict complex identity therefore gives the canonical natural isomorphism $R\Gamma(W,K)\cong R\Gamma(\mathcal C/W,j_W^*K)$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$. Applying the cohomology functor in degree $q$ gives the stated isomorphism $H^qR\Gamma(W,K)\cong H^qR\Gamma(\mathcal C/W,j_W^*K)$ for every integer $q$, with no boundedness restriction.
